payload.red_observed:
EVERY NEW CHECK, WITH ITS OBSERVED FAILURE. A check that has never been seen red is a check that might assert nothing, so each is recorded with HOW it was made to fail and WHAT it said.

AN HONEST STATEMENT OF ORDER FIRST. This state's guidance says red is observed before any code lands. That did not happen for most of this iteration, and the reason is a ruling rather than an oversight: the owner ordered the round injection built immediately and the iteration re-walked afterwards. So for the chunks built before the rewalk, red was observed at the moment the check was written — against code that already existed — by DISABLING the behaviour rather than by predating it. That is weaker evidence than test-first, and I am naming the weakness rather than presenting the observations as if they came in the canonical order.

== RED OBSERVED BY DISABLING THE FIX — the strongest form available here ==

THE REOPEN PROPERTIES (two checks). Run run-dc658660000e, three configurations of the same suite:
  Both fixes on: 4 pass, 0 fail.
  Re-arm disabled: 3 pass, 1 FAIL — 'stranded — log_risks->gate_motivation was consumed and never restored'.
  Self-fuel guard disabled: 2 pass, 2 FAIL — 'a reopened state completes and MOVES ON' and the reachability property, both naming re-activation.
  WHY THIS IS THE BEST EVIDENCE IN THE SET: the two disabled behaviours are the two defects that actually happened today. The check was not shown to fail on an invented fault — it was shown to fail on the exact faults it exists to prevent, one at a time.

THE CONSOLE-WINDOW LINT. Observed red on its FIRST RUN, without any deliberate breakage: 0 pass, 1 fail, naming engine/search.ts:77 — a call site the hand sweep had missed, and the most frequently called of all. A check that finds a real defect the moment it is written has proved it asserts something.

THE PROMOTION'S SUITE RUNNER (empty-run and no-files-found). Observed red by construction before the fix: the promotion refused three times reporting a red suite while trunk was green, because the runner counted a crashed module resolution as one failing test named after the directory. The check that now asserts a real runner run was written against that observed behaviour.

THE GATE-ROUNDS PROPERTY. Observed red INDIRECTLY and at scale: when the injection landed, eight fixture-gate tests went red at once, because the machine began refusing gate submissions without rounds. That is the same assertion from the other side — the machine's refusal is what the property now asserts statically. I did not separately disable the injection to watch this specific check fail, and I am recording that gap rather than implying I did.

THE BINARY-EXCLUSION TEST. Observed red in the PROBE rather than in the suite: run-9406dd97f88c showed version-control grep, without the flag, emitting 'Binary file bin.dat matches' as a line with no field structure — one field where the parser expects three. The test asserts what that line would break. I did not remove the flag from the engine to watch the suite go red, because the flag is in the shared judge and removing it would have exposed the live lane; the probe result is the evidence, and it is weaker than a suite-level red by exactly one step.

== RED OBSERVED IN THE ORDINARY WAY, before the code ==

THE PROPERTY TEST'S OWN FIRST RUN. Worth recording because it cuts against me: the reachability property failed on its first run naming 54 stranded states — and the fault was in the TEST, not the engine. Its invariant applied to the directly-reopened states, which are activated by the reopen and need no fuel. A property test is a claim too, and it has to be read as sceptically as the code it judges. Fixed, then observed red again under the deliberate disabling above.

THE REQUIRED-ARGUMENT GUARD. Observed red twice, in both directions, which is why the check now has two halves: first a wrong argument name made search hunt for the literal word 'undefined' and return confident irrelevant hits; then the guard built to stop that REFUSED a legitimate explicitly-empty value, and the check asserting that absent and empty are different was written against that second observed failure.

== WHAT IS NOT HERE, and why ==
No check exists for the applicability join, so none was observed red. Its chunk is drawn as blocked. A green check with no realized design is suspect; an ABSENT check with no realized design is at least honest, and it is what the record shows.
